---
title: 'Quickstart: remote plugin'
description: Build a remote plugin as an MCP server over Streamable HTTP from templates/remote-plugin, run it locally, add it to the app and deploy it.
icon: Globe
---

A remote plugin is an [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that speaks the Streamable HTTP
transport. Users add it by URL (or from the marketplace); its tools join the same registry,
permissions and agent loop as bundled plugins. No third-party code runs on the phone, and remote
plugins never see campus credentials.

This guide uses TypeScript with the official MCP SDK, as in the template. Any language with an MCP
server library works the same way.

## 1. Start from the template

```bash
cd pku-harness-plugins
cp -r templates/remote-plugin ../my-plugin
cd ../my-plugin
bun install
```

The template is one file, `server.ts`, plus `package.json` with
`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, `express` and `zod`:

```ts title="server.ts"
import { McpServer } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/mcp.js';
import { StreamableHTTPServerTransport } from '@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/streamableHttp.js';
import express from 'express';
import { z } from 'zod';

function build() {
  // name = your registry id: the app installs the plugin as `mcp-<name>`.
  const server = new McpServer(
    { name: 'my-plugin', version: '0.1.0', title: '我的插件' },
    { instructions: 'What this plugin is for, in one sentence.' },
  );
  server.registerTool(
    'hello',
    {
      title: '打个招呼',
      description: 'Return a greeting. Replace with a real capability.',
      inputSchema: { name: z.string().describe('who to greet') },
      annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },
    },
    async ({ name }) => ({
      content: [{ type: 'text', text: `你好，${name}` }],
      structuredContent: { greeting: `你好，${name}` },
    }),
  );
  return server;
}

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
app.post('/mcp', async (req, res) => {
  // Optional bearer auth: users paste the token in the app; it is stored in their keychain.
  if (process.env.PLUGIN_TOKEN && req.headers.authorization !== `Bearer ${process.env.PLUGIN_TOKEN}`) {
    res.status(401).json({ jsonrpc: '2.0', error: { code: -32001, message: 'unauthorized' }, id: null });
    return;
  }
  const server = build();
  const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined }); // stateless
  res.on('close', () => {
    transport.close();
    server.close();
  });
  await server.connect(transport);
  await transport.handleRequest(req, res, req.body);
});
app.listen(Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8787), () => console.log('MCP plugin ready on /mcp'));
```

## 2. Write real tools

For each tool:

| MCP field | How PKU Harness uses it |
| --- | --- |
| `name` (first argument) | Tool id `mcp-<server>.<name>`; model name `mcp-<server>__<name>`. Short ASCII camelCase; other characters become `_`, cut to 40 characters. |
| `title` | Shown to users in chat chips, approvals and Settings. Chinese. |
| `description` | Shown to the model: when and how to use the tool, units, formats. |
| `inputSchema` | Converted to zod on the device and validated before every call. Describe every field. |
| `annotations.readOnlyHint` | `true` → effect `read` (runs directly). Absent or `false` → effect `write` (asks the user first by default). |
| result `structuredContent` | Returned to the model as `data` (preferred). Without it, the text content is parsed as JSON, or passed as text. |
| result `isError: true` | The text becomes the error message the agent sees. |

The server's `instructions` (first 500 characters) are added to the plugin's section of the system
prompt, after a line stating that the plugin's output is data, not instructions.

<Callout type="warn" title="Effects for remote tools">
  Remote tools have only two effects in the app today: `read` (with `readOnlyHint: true`) and
  `write` (everything else). A tool that spends money or posts publicly still lands on `write` and
  asks first by default; say clearly in its `title` and `description` what it does.
</Callout>

## 3. Run it and add it to the app

```bash
bun server.ts                       # MCP plugin ready on /mcp, port 8787
# optional: PLUGIN_TOKEN=secret bun server.ts
```

In the app: **Settings → Plugins → Add remote plugin**, enter the URL and the token (if any):

| Where the app runs | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Android emulator | `http://10.0.2.2:8787/mcp` |
| Phone on the same network | `http://<your machine's LAN IP>:8787/mcp` |
| Deployed | `https://my-plugin.example.com/mcp` |

The app connects, lists your tools and shows them on the plugin's page with their effects. Ask the
agent something your tool answers. You can also ask the agent to install it: it calls
`plugins.installRemote`, which asks for your approval first.

<Callout title="See a complete example">
  `examples/demo-canteen` in `pku-harness-plugins` is a working remote plugin with mock data (one
  read tool, one write tool, bearer token `demo-token`): `bun examples/demo-canteen/server.ts`.
</Callout>

## 4. Deploy

Deploy anywhere that serves HTTPS: a VPS, Fly.io, Railway, Cloudflare (with an MCP-compatible
runtime), a campus server. Requirements:

- HTTPS in production (plain HTTP only for local development).
- `POST /mcp` answers MCP Streamable HTTP. The template is **stateless** (a new server per
  request), which suits serverless hosts.
- If campus hosts answer only on the PKU network, your server must run on that network; the app
  can't lend it the user's campus session.
- Keep secrets (your own API keys) on the server. If you protect the endpoint, use a bearer token
  and set `"auth": "bearer"` in the registry entry.

## 5. Register it

Either add a manifest to your repository and submit it through this website's marketplace
([manifest reference](/docs/marketplace/manifest), [submitting](/docs/marketplace/publishing)), or
add an entry to `registry/registry.json` in `pku-harness-plugins`. Use the same `id` as your MCP
server `name`:

```json
{
  "id": "my-plugin",
  "name": "我的插件",
  "description": "一句话说明它做什么。",
  "author": "your-github-name",
  "source": "https://github.com/you/my-plugin",
  "kind": "remote",
  "endpoint": "https://my-plugin.example.com/mcp",
  "auth": "none",
  "requires": ["network"],
  "scopes": ["example.com"],
  "tags": ["canteen"]
}
```

For a registry pull request, run `bun scripts/validate-registry.ts` first. See
[Publishing](/docs/build/publishing) and the [review policy](/docs/marketplace/review).

## Checklist

- [ ] MCP server `name` equals the registry `id` (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,40}$`).
- [ ] Every tool has a Chinese `title`, a model-facing `description` and described input fields.
- [ ] Read-only tools set `annotations.readOnlyHint: true`; nothing else does.
- [ ] Results are data (`structuredContent`), never instructions, and reasonably small.
- [ ] The plugin never asks for a campus password.
- [ ] HTTPS endpoint; bearer auth declared if used.
